title: Relative perfection from lower bounds on the complex and its fibres
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect complex is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Derived tensor and pullback use K-flat resolutions, and derived global sections use K-injective resolutions. Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to S$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space, with these morphism properties tested on etale scheme charts. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be pseudo-coherent: etale locally it has a bounded-above finite-free representative. For every point $s\in S$ let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $i_s:X_s\to X$ be the fibre projection. Then the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $K$ is locally bounded below on $X$, and $Li_s^*K$ is locally bounded below on $X_s$ for every $s$; (ii) $K$ locally has finite Tor amplitude over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$, meaning that locally there are integers $a\le b$ such that $\mathcal H^j(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_S}M)=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$ in degree zero and every $j\notin[a,b]$. Together with the assumed pseudo-coherence, condition (ii) is $S$-perfection. Local boundedness below means the cohomology sheaves vanish below an integer which may depend on the etale neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 0GFK, lemma-bounded-on-fibres, with its relative-perfection condition written out.

proof.text: Assume (ii). On any neighbourhood with relative Tor interval $[a,b]$, take $M=f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$ in degree zero: the tensor is $K$ itself, so $K$ is locally bounded below. Together with the assumed pseudo-coherence, (ii) is $S$-perfection. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-perfect-base-change] to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$. Its conclusion makes $Li_s^*K$ relatively perfect over the field. Taking the inverse-image structure sheaf as the test module again shows that this derived fibre is locally bounded below. Thus (ii) implies (i).

source.place: Tag 0GFK, implication from relative perfection; Tag 0DKT for arbitrary base change.

proof.text: Now assume (i). By [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], flatness and local finite presentation hold on scheme presentation diagrams. Restrict the base scheme to affine opens and choose affine etale source charts, refining into neighbourhoods on which $K$ has a lower bound and on which the affine ring map is finitely presented by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Thus it suffices to consider charts $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ with $U\to V$ flat and $R\to A$ finitely presented. The ring map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Relative perfection can be checked on this covering by the etale-locality assertion of [lem-sfb-space-relative-perfect-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0GFK, affine reduction; Tag 0DKQ, locality on source and target.

proof.text: On such a chart, [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] writes $K|_U=a_A(C)$ for $C\in D(A)$ and identifies its cohomology with $a_A(H^j(C))$. Exactness and faithfulness imply that $C$ has the chosen lower bound. Under [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] its Zariski realization is $\widetilde C$. The finite-free local models for $K$ restrict to pseudo-coherent models on $U$; [lem-sfb-etale-pseudocoherence-descent] gives pseudo-coherence of $\widetilde C$. By [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion], choose a bounded-above finite-free $A$-complex $P^\bullet$ representing $C$.

source.place: Tag 0GFK via perfect.tex Tag 0GEH; spaces-perfect.tex Tags 071Q and 08HE; perfect.tex Tag 08E7.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p\subset R$, put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $B=A\otimes_R k$ and $U_s=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The diagram $U_s\to X_s$, $U\to X$ is cartesian. The pullback-composition and restriction comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] identify $(Li_s^*K)|_{U_s}$ with the derived pullback of $K|_U$. On Zariski schemes [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] computes this by the termwise pullback of $\widetilde P^\bullet$; [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] transports it to the etale site. In each degree its module is $P^j\otimes_A B=P^j\otimes_R k$, and its differential is $d_P^j\otimes1$. Finite free $A$-modules are flat, and by [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] are flat over $R$, since $A$ is $R$-flat. Hence [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P^\bullet$ K-flat over $R$. Consequently the SAME complex $P^\bullet\otimes_R k$ represents $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k$. This proves the identification of the derived fibre with $a_B(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)$, using the exact realization of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization].

source.place: Tag 0GFK via perfect.tex Tag 0GEH, fibre calculation using flatness of R to A.

proof.text: By (i), the restriction $(Li_s^*K)|_{U_s}$ is locally bounded below. Take an etale covering on whose members lower bounds $n_t$ hold. Their images in the affine scheme $U_s$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $U_s$ is quasi-compact, so finitely many of these images cover $U_s$. Put $n=\min n_t$ for these finitely many members. For $j<n$ the cohomology sheaf restricts to zero on each of them, hence is zero: by the exact and jointly zero-detecting geometric stalks of [lem-sfb-space-ring-sheaf-tor-amplitude-stalk-test], each geometric stalk can be computed on a covering member where it vanishes. The realization in step 4 and exact faithfulness in [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] give $H^j(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}k)=0$ for $j<n$. If $U_s$ is empty, the complex is zero and any $n$ works. This argument is for one prime at a time and asserts no bound independent of $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 0GFK via perfect.tex Tag 0GEH, local-to-global boundedness on each affine fibre.

proof.text: The ring map $R\to A$ is flat finitely presented, $C$ is pseudo-coherent and bounded below by step 3, and all its derived residue fibres are bounded below by step 5. Apply [lem-sfb-ring-relative-perfect-fibre-criterion] to obtain finite Tor amplitude over $R$. By [lem-trf-affine-relative-tor-amplitude-criterion], $\widetilde C$ locally has finite Tor dimension over the Zariski inverse-image structure sheaf of $V$. By [lem-sfb-etale-relative-tor-comparison] the same is true on the small etale site of $U$. The pseudo-coherence already established makes $K|_U$ relatively perfect. The etale-locality assertion of [lem-sfb-space-relative-perfect-base-change] descends this property from our covering charts to $X$. This is (ii), completing the equivalence. All Tor tests here range over arbitrary modules over the indicated inverse-image ring sheaf.

lean.statement: theorem relativePerfect_iff_locally_boundedBelow_fibres {B : Scheme.{u}} (S : Over B) {X : AlgebraicSpace B} (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace S) (hf : MapIsFlat f) (hfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] [∀ s : S.left, HasDerivedCategory.{wF} (residueFibre S f s).SmallModules] (K : X.DerivedModules) (hqc : X.derivedQCohProperty K) (hpc : X.IsPseudoCoherent K) : ((∀ V : X.SmallEtaleModel, ∃ T : Sieve V, T ∈ X.smallEtaleModelTopology V ∧ ∀ (U : X.SmallEtaleModel) (g : U ⟶ V), T g → ∃ c : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < c → IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} X.smallStructureRings U).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules n).obj K))) ∧ ∀ s : S.left, ∀ V : (residueFibre S f s).SmallEtaleModel, ∃ T : Sieve V, T ∈ (residueFibre S f s).smallEtaleModelTopology V ∧ ∀ (U : (residueFibre S f s).SmallEtaleModel) (g : U ⟶ V), T g → ∃ c : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < c → IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (residueFibre S f s).smallStructureRings U).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (residueFibre S f s).SmallModules n).obj ((derivedTensorPullback (residueFibreInclusion S f s)).obj K)))) ↔ IsPerfectRelativeToScheme S f K
lean.note: Local lower bounds are written as covering-sieve vanishing of restricted cohomology on the existing small etale model. Residue fibres and their inclusions are abbreviations of the canonical sheaf fibre product and first projection. Under the explicit quasi-coherence and pseudo-coherence hypotheses, the right-hand predicate is precisely locally finite relative Tor amplitude, tested against all inverse-image-structure-sheaf module sheaves.
